entries.title: Build-stamped Cloud endpoint manifest committed to the repository
entries.description: Commit 8c14569 committed cloud-endpoints.json with channel='staging', violating the manifest's own documented contract (packaging stamps the channel at build time; the committed default is development). This broke apps/desktop/test/cloud-endpoint.test.ts 'parses the committed repository manifest' (suite went 2453 passed / 1 failed at HEAD 63fa479, contradicting the certified 0-failed claim) and pointed non-packaged developer checkouts at the staging Cloud origin instead of the local development server.
entries.generalCause: A release-preparation step mutated a tracked source file instead of a build-local copy, and the change was not re-verified against the full suite before certification evidence was recorded.
entries.fix: Restored the committed manifest to channel='development' while keeping the staging endpoint entry recorded for the known staging deployment (commit c217e96).
entries.regressionCoverage: apps/desktop/test/cloud-endpoint.test.ts (existing test detected the regression; restored to green).

entries.title: Deterministic verification gate cannot pass real monorepo suites (300s per-command ceiling, no override)
entries.description: runVerification enforces a 300s per-command timeout and no caller could override it. This repository's own full 'npm test' runs ~15-20 minutes, so any autonomous run whose verification command is a real monorepo suite has that command killed into a fabricated failure and the run terminates blocked with VERIFICATION_FAILED.
entries.generalCause: A defensive default timeout was made non-configurable; the verification-service comment acknowledged long real suites but no opt-in path existed.
entries.fix: Added caller-opt-in verificationTimeoutMs to OrchestratorRunOptions, forwarded to runVerification (commit bf6bc14). Default unchanged (300s) for every existing path; the corpus runner passes 45 minutes for monorepo-suite oracles.
entries.regressionCoverage: The corpus itself is the regression proof: every CodeForge npm-test task exercises the raised ceiling (its oracle requires >15 minutes of verification). The default ceiling remains covered by existing verification-service timeout tests.

entries.title: Oracle wrapper spawned npx.cmd without a shell (spawn EINVAL on Node >= 20.12)
entries.description: The corpus oracle wrapper invoked npx.cmd via child_process.execFile without shell:true; Node's post-CVE-2024-27980 restriction rejects spawning .cmd/.bat without an explicit shell, so every verification command died with spawn EINVAL. The S-001 smoke test caught it before campaign execution: the run honestly terminated blocked (VERIFICATION_FAILED) and was classified FAILED with no false completion. The same defect had already been fixed in the runner's freeze path but was missed in the wrapper.
entries.generalCause: Windows .cmd shims cannot be spawned directly by Node after the 20.12 security patch; every spawn site must go through a shell or invoke the underlying JS entry with process.execPath.
entries.fix: The wrapper now invokes node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs through process.execPath (no shell shim involved).
entries.regressionCoverage: The S-001 corpus run is the regression proof: its verification command exercises the wrapper end-to-end through the pipeline. Smoke evidence archived at corpus-runs/campaign-1/smoke-archive/S-001-wrapper-eval.

entries.title: Runner classified managed-free daily-capacity exhaustion as FAILED instead of CAPACITY_BLOCKED
entries.description: When Groq's daily TPD bucket (200,000 tokens for openai/gpt-oss-120b) exhausted mid-run, the explorers failed with PROVIDER_RATE_LIMITED, ForgeZero marked the provider unhealthy provider-wide (certified semantics), and the planner truthfully received PROVIDER_MODEL_UNAVAILABLE. The runner classified the run FAILED (run_blocked) because it only scanned the run summary for capacity keywords, not the turn-level failure events; the second S-001 smoke attempt was therefore misclassified.
entries.generalCause: Classification relied on the run's top-level summary text; provider health cascades surface the capacity cause only in worker telemetry (providerFailures) and turn.failed events.
entries.fix: The runner now persists turn.failed/subagent.failed error strings per attempt and classifies a blocked run as CAPACITY_BLOCKED when rate-limit/TPD markers appear in failure events, or when PROVIDER_MODEL_UNAVAILABLE coincides with providerFailures > 0. A PROVIDER_MODEL_UNAVAILABLE with zero provider failures remains a genuine FAILED routing defect. Also fixed worker request-count aggregation (modelRequests field).
entries.regressionCoverage: Smoke evidence archived at corpus-runs/campaign-1/smoke-archive/S-001-capacity-exhausted (the misclassified attempt); the S-001 run executed after this fix is the regression proof of the corrected classification.

entries.title: Model-scoped daily-quota 429 marked provider-wide as a transient rate limit, destroying within-provider failover
entries.description: On any 429 during real inference, agent-runtime marked EVERY model of the provider rate_limited (retryAfter now+60s). A TPD 429 (model-scoped daily token wall, observed verbatim: Groq openai/gpt-oss-120b Limit 200000/day) therefore (a) cooled down sibling models (gpt-oss-20b, qwen) that shared nothing but the organization, removing within-provider failover exactly when the primary wall hit, and (b) classified a until-midnight condition as a 60-second transient. In window 1 of the frozen R3 corpus this cascade contributed to 25 of 90 attempts failing with provider_health_marked_unavailable and to zero-capacity runs continuing to be dispatched against a dead fleet.
entries.generalCause: Failure classification was keyed on the transport signal (429) only, ignoring the quota scope the provider states in the 429 body; the health-marking API only supported provider-wide marking.
entries.fix: Added classifyProviderFailure/planFailureHealthMarking (packages/forge-zero/src/health-classify.ts): daily-signal 429 bodies classify model-scoped quota_exhausted with retryAfter at the next 00:00 UTC reset; other 429s classify model-scoped rate_limited with bounded cooldown (default 60s, Retry-After honored, 15 min cap); auth failures remain provider-scoped (credential is org-wide); 5xx/overload remains provider-scoped bounded degraded. ForgeZero.markModelHealth marks a single model. agent-runtime failure path now applies the scoped marking.
entries.regressionCoverage: packages/forge-zero/test/health-classify.test.ts: 12 tests including model-scoped sibling-eligibility, provider-wide auth cascade, cooldown expiry, and no-guessing on unclassified errors.

entries.title: quota_exhausted health state could never auto-restore at daily quota reset
entries.description: verifyProviderAccount hard-excluded quota_exhausted with no expiry path: once a route was marked quota-exhausted it stayed unroutable until process restart or manual re-discovery, violating the §33 requirement that quota reset should restore eligibility automatically. This made the FR-005 fix impossible without also changing the verifier: the correct quota marking (until daily reset) would otherwise have been a permanent ban.
entries.generalCause: The health state enum carried a quota_exhausted status with retryAfter support in the schema, but the verifier never consumed retryAfter for that status.
entries.fix: quota_exhausted is now excluded only until its marked retryAfter (daily-window reset); without a marked reset time it remains excluded (fail closed). Auto-restore covered by test.
entries.regressionCoverage: packages/forge-zero/test/health-classify.test.ts (auto-restore at reset; fail-closed without reset time).

entries.title: Oracle wrapper reported vitest produced no parseable JSON report in the worktree (verification blocked a review-passed candidate)
entries.description: S-001 attempt 2 (simple, oracle npm test): 52 real model requests through cloudflare-workers-ai/@cf/openai/gpt-oss-120b (fleet rotated from Groq — cross-provider failover worked). Independent Code Reviewer PASSED; integration verification failed with oracle-wrapper: vitest produced no parseable JSON report. The gate honestly blocked the run (false_completion=false), but the verification harness could not evaluate a candidate that reached the verification stage, so the task failed on harness plumbing rather than task merit.
entries.generalCause: Under investigation: the wrapper JSON reporter may not be wired in the worktree vitest invocation, or vitest crashed before producing a report (Windows worktree node_modules junction / reporter registration).
entries.fix: OPEN — needs reproduction with the preserved attempt evidence (tests/evidence/r3/corpus-runs/campaign-1/evidence/S-001/attempt-2).

entries.title: Planner completed without an authorized task graph; orchestrator honestly blocked the run
entries.description: S-002 attempt 2 (simple): 28 real model requests through cloudflare-workers-ai/@cf/openai/gpt-oss-120b. The planner turn reported completion but its output was not an authorized task graph, so the run terminated blocked (Planner did not produce an authorized task graph). No fabricated completion; gate blocked before coder/reviewer. Likely planner-structured-output robustness against the Cloudflare-served gpt-oss-120b response shape.
entries.generalCause: Under investigation: planner structured-output contract enforcement vs the Cloudflare-served model output (fenced JSON extraction exists; the planner output may have been valid prose or a schema-violating graph).
entries.fix: OPEN — needs reproduction with preserved evidence (tests/evidence/r3/corpus-runs/campaign-1/evidence/S-002/attempt-2).
